CHAPTER VII RECOMMENDATION
After a thorough review of the findings associated with environmental review and the comments received it has been determined that the project should be approved. The recommendation is based upon the obvious conclusion that while a significant environment impact exists it is an overwhelmingly favorable impact.
Following the findings of the environmental review process the Department of Pousing and Urban Development will require the following modifications and/or additions to project proposals as a condition for approval.
1. The Urban Renewal Plan and project improvements schedule will be revised at the City's earliest covenience but no later than prior to disposition of any affected project land in order to conform to the suggested actions as outlined in Chapter II, paragraph A.6.c.(6) as to landscaped berm and wall shield requirements.
2. The Richmond Redevelopment and Housing Authority through paragraph C.2.a.(8) 'Right of Review' of the Urban Renewal Plan will fully implement the required design modifications i.e. crientation of living areas, acoustically treated window and door openings, etc. as described in the statement as necessary techniques in the expressway effected areas. The Authority will document their review of such factors and their findings and will maintain such documentation for public review upon appropriate request.
3. The Richmond Redevelopment and Housing Authority will through the project associated housing rehabilitation standards and program provide assistance in determining noise attentutation measures necessary for noise effected rehabilitation structures. The Authority will provide technical as well as financial assistance for the required improvements to the same degree as any other basic rehabilitation improvement considered eligible for either a loan or grant.
4. The Richmond Redevelopment and Housing Authority and the Department of Housing and Urban Development will monitor air quality conditions in the proposed project area noting any significant changes resulting from increased traffic in and through the project area. If necessary an evaluation of air quality problems will be made at that time with corrective actions taking advantage of the latest technology studied and implement to the maximum extent practical.
